_meta.notes: Agency products, not press coverage — the news view keeps them in their own strip. Every item carries the date its agency published it, parsed from the page; an undated item is dropped rather than stamped with the collection time. Items past their cadence are flagged stale rather than hidden. NOAA Climate.gov's ENSO blog is probed every run and deliberately excluded: it returns 200 with a fresh Last-Modified while its newest post is more than a year old.

bulletins.title: Weekly relative Niño 3.4 +2.53 °C, Troup SOI -19.5 (30 days to 23 Sep)
bulletins.summary: BoM's operational ocean index for the week ending 20 September 2026. Its El Niño threshold is +0.8 °C, higher than CPC's +0.5. The SOI is negative, the El Niño-like sign, so the atmosphere is coupled to the ocean signal.

bulletins.title: September 2026 Quick Look · ENSO forecast
bulletins.summary: The IRI/CPC plume and the consensus probabilistic forecast, issued monthly. This is the forecast the page's own outlook language is checked against.

bulletins.title: Earth has hottest August on record
ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory
bulletins.summary: El Niño is strengthening, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter 2026-27. El Niño strengthened further over the past month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +3. The monthly ENSO Diagnostic Discussion, issued on the second Thursday.

bulletins.title: El Niño Outlook, September 2026 to March 2027
bulletins.summary: El Niño conditions are considered to have persisted in the equatorial Pacific since Spring 2026. They are virtually certain (100%) to continue until boreal winter. Japan's monthly outlook, issued around the tenth.
